# T44 records-only close-out retro — 2026-11-03

Owner #691; audit #1413; interface epic #700. Authority: full #691 comment6591582676 and stream v2 at821de9d39378b091c9d55a2f68734d8a36d65613. S1 documentary commit d0274e2de5d8af353f8643798491ad8c126da73f. Actual executor Codex/openai/gpt-6-astra/openai/xhigh, own observed Herdr footer (UI observation, not provider attestation), session01a19d12-1c5f-7022-8053-102f6a94b7fe, wN:p5. Local reviewers[] remain unchanged.

## What changed and what was learned

PL001 resolves the carrying-decision documentation only. Temporary retention of doctest2.4.12 preserves the accepted harness substrate while an update is evaluated on a separately pinned current integration tree. Observing official2.5.3 on2026-11-02 supplies currency context, not compatibility proof or a reason to relabel accepted tests. Revisit at the next doctest/toolchain/test-harness change or before vendored-library upstream submission, whichever comes first; confirmed defects trigger owner triage. No release-readiness waiver follows.

#1414 retains five unchecked future groups: doctest complete consumer/compiler/allowed-failure mapping with T18#665 and T2#649/T34#681/T35#682; rcheevos R13 dual12.2.1/10.7.0 mapping and dated12.5.0 applicability with T20#667's excluded hash/RVZ/three-hasher work; libretro-common mixed subset with T20's excluded MD5/hash; NanoSVG import/optimization mapping with T36#683; id3v2lib flattened import/current revision and library/vendor-test mapping with T37#684. #1414 remains open under #700/M6. Examples do not exhaust consumers; missing upstream inputs remain missing.

Native594, separate3tests/450lines and four companions remain separate evidence populations. Primary ES55158 contains T2 PL024; French T2/T21/T34/T35/T36 counts3/6/1/1/0 do not describe a combined accepted source tree. #700 owns future companion integration. Pugixml system recipe and uninitialized gitlink remain distinct. #256, #585 and existing behavioral bugs retain their owners.

## Evidence limitations that remain explicit

1. Historical records.py SHA2566858cf1cb719839b3d0e16c9976c847e0abbe3c07e2797abeab0931fdaeb2cee is retained in stage-d/pre-issue-1/records.py. Current records.py SHAc6bf939816cb15c0b7bb0d7a5d241ab89e70c5dcda1ea1572682ba497294db5b differs only in the scorecard heading. A new immutable binding preserves both; the old hash stays old.
2. Earlier D lints/gates predate final00/02/06 and certify snapshot/pre-issue scope only. Later document readback/index-2/syntax-3/diff-3 bind their own inputs. New E/F record checks cannot retroactively certify old final bytes.
3. An ignored Python bytecode file caused the original manifest failure. Exit1/diagnostic survive; full original argv/times/raw-stream hashes do not. The later bound MANIFEST_KEYSET refusal is separate. Python now uses -I -B; -I ignores the environment bytecode setting. The ignored file remains in the bounded custody census pending sufficiently bound retirement, not silently deleted.
4. D worklog-index-write.receipt.json lacks stderr hash/file. That absence remains explicit.

First publicationd6d08 and correctedD923dd remain distinct; accepted producer programs and receipts are frozen.

## New record-only controls and corrections

The frozen D guard lacks the new retro/date paths. A separately named E-H guard binds an exact date allowlist and protects every commit, the seed-to-tip delta, all268 noneditable D artifacts, source/selector/rule identities, and whole clean ES identity. Ten new refusals and a positive include product edit-then-revert, frozen-record drift, unrelated retro/worklog, symlink/executable mode, deletion/rename and ES drift. Tiny synthetic Git contains no product source.

The first new receipt runner used git write-tree for an index observation. Parallel initializations contended for index.lock before four intended checks started. The original runner and partial scopes remain retained with their limits; no lock was removed or missing raw diagnostics reconstructed. A read-only index-entry SHA256 replaces it. Separate synthetic rc7/rc0 controls verify exit and both stream hashes. This correction concerns new record machinery, not an accepted producer.

A new raw heading-diff file and its whitespace diagnostic contain context spaces. The initial diff check really returned2. Both exact raw byte streams are retained externally and losslessly JSON-encoded in the committed record; the original failure receipt remains. The corrected record representation passes diff checking. No accepted artifact was normalized.

## Learning and next ownership

Bind program versions separately from later editorial corrections. Keep command scopes explicit and use read-only identity operations in parallel readers. Carry decisions and compatibility evidence answer different questions. Unsupported scratch custody remains retained with exact paths and a next owner; an empty census is not the goal.

Both time-to-play quantities remain unmeasured. No accepted audit/test replay, source edit, build/compiler/guest/runtime, source export/acquisition, provider/reviewer/device/cloud action or permission response occurred. Normal distribution record hooks are used. #1413 and #691 remain open for root simulation/acceptance; no completion marker or slice closure is claimed. Rule changes and further execution remain coordinator-owned.
